title: Telemetry Quickview proxy and ephemeral sanitizer for on-call snapshots
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: On-call responders need a lightweight, low-noise 'quickview' for incident telemetry that can be safely shared externally (e.g., cross-team handoffs, support threads) without leaking PII or credentials. This PR introduces a telemetry quickview proxy service that assembles compact rollups and an ephemeral sanitize pipeline that redacts sensitive fields and truncates large payloads. Design: a small proxy (Go) that sits in front of the incident-bundle API and returns a compact JSON summary containing metrics rollups, top traces, and sanitized logs. A sanitization blacklist/whitelist drives tokenization and redaction rules; heuristics trim long stack traces and canonicalize timestamp formats. The proxy emits a short checksum so recipients can verify bundle integrity without full data. The implementation includes an optional ephemeral mode (30-minute TTL links) suitable for cross-team sharing. Security and privacy: default deny on all fields; explicit allow-list for safe attributes. Sanitizer uses deterministic redaction (consistent placeholders per incident) so multiple quickviews can be correlated without exposing original values. All outgoing quickview links are audit-logged and optionally routed through the audit-log-exporter. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated behind incident-bot.experimental.quickview, staged rollout to N teams, opt-in via oncall console. Backwards compatibility: quickview is additive; standard incident-bundle endpoints are unchanged. Tests: unit tests for sanitizer heuristics, integration test harness that runs the proxy against stored incident fixtures, e2e smoke test validating TTL and audit logging. Usage: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://incident-bot.internal/quickview/<incident-id>?ttl=30m returns a compact JSON. Implementation notes: sanitizer rules are YAML-driven and live in config/sanitizer_rules.yaml; proxy has a small LRU cache for recent quickviews to reduce load during noisy incidents. Related work: builds on earlier ephemeral snapshot effort (ENG-4210) and interacts with the audit-log-exporter and oncall-clipboard changes. Checklist: updated docs, tests, feature-flag, security review completed. See release notes for operator toggles and default policies.

review_comments: Maya Nguyen: Security review: reducer patterns look good but please tighten default allowlist to exclude 'user.email' and 'auth.token' fields - done in last commit.

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: quickview default is disabled in production until policy signoff.
